Posted August 8, 2007

Analysis by Richard Cowan

 

As I was saying when I was so rudely interrupted From 2005:

Cannabis Prohibition Is Low-Intensity Warfare Against Social Peace, Individual Freedom and the Rule of Law. Be very afraid... Three Lessons.

and

Lets Play 'Connect the Dots' Again. Legalization In Denver and Riots In Paris. The Total Disconnect Between the Old Media and the Culture of the Internet. Dont Be An American Idiot.   

(Also see the personal note at the end.)

One thing that has not really changed in the last year or so: The Drug War is still largely ignored by the Left. (I will have plenty to say about the Right in due course. But it is only fair to judge people by their own standards, and what they supposedly consider to be important. And I would be the first to say that there are those on the Left who are doing an excellent job, especially Fred Gardner.)

See
Write Off Your Congressman
and

Prohibitionists Attack, Reformers Fundraise

and

Who's Afraid of Cannabidiol?



Even though the new threats to civil liberties in the War on Terror are often relatively minor in comparison with the longstanding abuses of the war on American cannabis users, including sick and dying medical marijuana users the anti-war blogosphere and the mainstream Liberal media critics of the Iraq war never seems to notice what is going on -- literally under their noses.

See

The Patriot Act Hits A New Low As The Prison/Probation/Parole Population Hits A New High.

and

Bush Should Have John Comical Ali Walters Explain The Iraq War, Then The Media Would Never Ask Any Embarrassing Questions. Doctrine Of Drug Czar Infallibility? Blame Canada, Again.



I hate it when I am right!

And when I am wrong!

See

Unintended Consequences: How The Iraq War Has Changed the Global Climate for Cannabis Prohibition. Analysis by Richard Cowan

Maximizing the potential of the Internet, anti-war bloggers can cite every lie and failed prediction pushed by advocates of the Iraq war, but only the libertarians, notably at Reason, and the Future of Freedom Foundation make the connection between the Drug War and the so-called War on Terror.

On MSNBC, Keith Olbermann excoriates the Bush Administration for its lies and incompetence, and delights in mocking the buffoonery of Gonzo Gonzalez, but never mentions the DEA, which he controls. Nor does his coverage of the US Attorneys fiasco extend to the real abuses of federal power in California and other medical marijuana states.

 

I wrote about this three years ago.

From 2004 see

Its The Stupidity, Stupid. How the Prohibitionist Ideology Has Wrecked The Republican Party and Undermined Democracy Everywhere. When Ideology Trumps Reality, The Result is Stupidity.

Consider this item from the July 27th Press Enterprise:

President Bush's nominee to become U.S.  attorney for the Inland and Los Angeles areas appeared to take the federal government's campaign against medical marijuana to a new level early this year.

Tom O'Brien, currently chief of the criminal division for the U.S.  attorney's office in Los Angeles, told members of the Coachella Valley Association of Governments on Jan. 8 that government officials could be prosecuted for allowing medical-marijuana dispensaries to operate.

In other words, a federal prosecutor persecutes the sick and dying, threatens an unprecedented new area of prosecution against elected local officials, who are acting under state law, runs roughshod over federalism and states rights and is rewarded with a promotion to US Attorney. And this isnt national news?? Because its about marijuana? Giggle, giggle

Then, this weekend I went to see Sicko, Michael Moores latest polemic, which is supposedly about the disgraceful state of the DEAland health care system. Most of what he said is simply off-topic for MarijuanaNews, so I will leave that to others, but what he did not say confirms the wisdom of Jose Marti, the Cuban national hero, who said, He who does not see things in their depth should not call himself a radical.

For example, Moore thought it worthwhile to report that the French government provides laundry services for new mothers, but he could not find the time to report that millions of Americans with chronic pain problems cannot get relief from their suffering because of the Drug War with or without insurance.

See

What Is More Important, Prohibition Or The Patients? The Death of Cheryl Miller Should Remind Us All To Demand A Change In Priorities. Should Pain Be A Crime?

and

We Have Already Won A Lot From The Supreme Court Case, Which Is Good Because That Is Probably All That We Are Going To Get. DEA Changes The Rules on Treating Pain.

Moore cleverly pointed out that prisoners at Guantamo get better treatment than many Americans, including heroic 9/11 rescue workers who are suffering from their exposure to pollution resulting from their work on the World TradeCenter ruins.

However, since the Afghan invasion I have heard far more concern from the Left about the condition of the Guantamo prisoners and those in Iraq  than about the condition of the 2.5 million Americans in the worlds largest Gulag.

See

Abuse In Prisons: Iraqi and American. Bush says, That is not the way we do things in America. No, That Is Exactly The Way We Do Things in America! Especially In Texas and Florida.

Moore also interviewed people who were being impoverished by the cost of prescription drugs, but his idea of rights never extends beyond the idea that the government should pay for everything.

The wisdom of that is again off-topic for MarijuanaNews, but there are millions of Americans who only want the government to stop interfering with their right to use a plant.

See

A Medical Marijuana User Says That "Marinol Rescheduling Is Worthless" For Him. He Simply Cannot Afford It. "My country is killing me."

Giving even more power to official medicine, under the guise of universal health care also has its risks.

See

Calling All Quacks: The Therapeutic Police State and the Politicization of Medicine. Doctors Cannot Study The Violence of Cannabis Prohibition. Because They Are The Disease, Not The Cure.

and

Live Free or Die In Pain. The Ignorance and Arrogance of the Quacks Who Deny Pain Relief to the Sick and Dying.

And  Ricky Williams and Our Paxil Problem. The Media Miss the Point, As Usual. "
..for the story that Michael Moore missed in Bowling for Columbine see

What If the Colorado Shooter Had Been Using Marijuana Instead Of A Pharmaceutical? Two Different Standards.

and

No, Cannabis Will Not Be The 21st Century Aspirin Because It Doesnt Kill Anyone! People Suffer And Die, While Scientists Try To Pharmaceuticalize The Aspirin Of the 21st Century B.C.

and

How Marijuana Prohibition Is Killing Darryl Strawberry And How Medical Marijuana Saved the Life of A Prominent UK Torys Son. Two Stories.

and

Meanwhile UK Painkillers Kill 2,000 Per Year. But They Are Sold Over-the-Counter So They Must Be Safe!

The supposedly progressive position on illegal drugs is that they are a public health problem, and drug abusers need treatment not jail. Consequently, it would be entirely appropriate to deal with this issue in the context of Sicko, but it is never even mentioned.

Of course, the Drug War creates other health problems, such as HIV infection among IV drug users and their sex partners. Hard drug addicts add to the burden of urban Emergency Rooms in their search for treatment for withdrawal and other problems. Prohibition related violence is also a major source of trauma in urban ERs.

While we should certainly be concerned about what we are NOT doing for the sick and dying at home and abroad, we should be ashamed of ourselves for what we are doing TO THEM, by denying them easy access to a plant that could alleviate their suffering.

Finally, it should be clear that easy access to medical cannabis would help millions of Americans, but the need is even greater in third world countries, including Cuba.

See

World AIDS Day: More Proof That the Suppression Of Medical Cannabis Indeed Cannabis Prohibition Itself Is Mass Murder. Analysis by Richard Cowan
